newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares open cautious, sideway shift seen.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares open cautious, sideway shift seen.

text.p: Singapore shares made a cautious start to the week on Monday, edging up slightly in early trade and dealers said the market was in consolidation mood.
"I think we're still moving rather sideways still and I expect the consolidation to continue," a dealer at a local brokerage said.
The barometer Straits Times Industrials Index was up 2.78 2,138.24 at 0240 GMT
Volume was a flimsy 45.4 million shares with losers ahead of gainers by 128 to 99.

Debut share Gul Technologies made the running in volume terms with 9.8 million shares traded by 0240 GMT to stand at S$0.805. The share hit a high of Singapore $0.90 in the opening minutes of trade, up 32 cents from its S$0.58 offer price.
Shares in conglomerate Keppel Corp also sparked interest, with 1.9 million units changing hands to lift the price S$0.15 to S$9.70.

Foreign share tranches led both early gainers and losers, Singapore Press foreign shares, up S$0.50 at S$27.10 and leading the gainers. Losers were headed by OUB Bank foreign shares, down S$0.30 at $10.50.
